name: lambda:UpdateFunctionCode WITHOUT iam:PassRole - standalone code-overwrite primitive, NOT a PassRole path
note: Updating an existing function's code runs under the function's already-attached execution role. Without iam:PassRole the principal cannot attach a MORE-privileged role, so no PASSROLE-* path fires - but overwriting the code of an existing (possibly privileged) function is itself a standalone code-execution / lateral-movement primitive (Stage-13 EFO-3), so LAMBDA-CODE-OVERWRITE fires at high.
rationale: lambda:UpdateFunctionCode changes the code of an EXISTING function, which executes under the execution role already attached to that function; it does not let the caller choose or attach a role. The PassRole family (which requires iam:PassRole to assign a privileged role to a new/updated workload) therefore must NOT fire. It is however a real standalone privilege-escalation / lateral-movement primitive on its own: attacker-supplied code runs under the existing function's role (Rhino 'UpdateExistingLambdaFunctionCode'). Whether that role is more privileged than the caller is unknown from this policy (out-of-scope target), which is why it is HIGH (evidence high, exploitability medium) rather than the compound critical PassRole path. Stage-13 EFO-3 reversed the earlier assumption that this was merely a lower-confidence non-finding: reading fully CLEAN on it was a T8 fail-open. Ref: AWS Lambda UpdateFunctionCode API; Lambda execution-role model.
